I am the Director of Research at the [International Growth Centre](https://www.theigc.org/) and a Research Fellow in Environmental Economics at the [London School of Economics](https://www.lse.ac.uk/). I hold a PhD in Economics from LSE.

My work sits at the intersection of environmental economics, development economics, and political economy. I advise governments across Asia and Africa on energy sector reform and public finance, and I lead IGC's research agenda on growth in low- and middle-income countries. Before joining IGC's research leadership, I worked as a Policy Economist across Bangladesh, Myanmar, Pakistan, and Afghanistan, and as IGC's Country Economist in Myanmar.

### Research Themes

**Energy transition in emerging markets** — Power sector reform, electrification, and the effects of energy access on development outcomes in Asia and Africa.

**Climate change and poverty** — How climate shocks and natural disasters affect the poor, and whether adaptation can keep pace with a changing climate.

**Political economy of development** — Political accountability, the role of mass media, deforestation and land use, and the institutions that shape growth.
